# Findings — calculator.aws estimate replay

**Verdict:** **Yes.** Populated `https://calculator.aws/#/estimate?id=...` share URLs can be generated by calling the calculator's backend directly with no browser, no AWS credentials, and no signing. A 30-line Python script using only `requests` is sufficient.

**Working share URL produced by the PoC during this spike:**
`https://calculator.aws/#/estimate?id=491f7f59c4d962ebf2291d935b3ec3f3f1555eb7` *(open in a browser to confirm the estimate renders)*

## Endpoints

| Purpose | Method | URL | Auth |
|---|---|---|---|
| Save estimate | `POST` | `https://dnd5zrqcec4or.cloudfront.net/Prod/v2/saveAs` | none |
| Load estimate | `GET`  | `https://d3knqfixx3sbls.cloudfront.net/{savedKey}` | none |
| Share URL | (client-built) | `https://calculator.aws/#/estimate?id={savedKey}` | n/a |

Both hosts are CloudFront distributions. `saveAs` is fronted by API Gateway with a Lambda proxy integration (envelope shape `{statusCode, body, isBase64Encoded, headers}`); the load host is a CloudFront → S3 read keyed by the `savedKey`. Confirmed via response headers (`X-Amz-Cf-Id`, `x-amz-apigw-id`, `Via: ... CloudFront`) in the captured HAR.

## Auth

**There is none.** The captured `POST` carries no `Authorization`, no `X-Api-Key`, no `X-Amz-Date`, no `X-Amz-Security-Token`, no Cognito identity, no SigV4 signature. The CORS preflight lists those header names in `Access-Control-Allow-Headers` as boilerplate — the server does not require them.

The only headers the SPA sends with semantic value are:

- `Content-Type: application/json`
- `Origin: https://calculator.aws`
- `Referer: https://calculator.aws/`

The PoC sends those plus a Chrome-ish `User-Agent`. Whether they are strictly required (vs. a bare `curl -X POST -H 'Content-Type: application/json'` working) was not exhaustively tested; matching the SPA defends against any CloudFront/WAF rules that might key on Origin or UA.

## Request schema (`POST /Prod/v2/saveAs`)

Top-level body shape:

```json
{
  "name": "<display name, free-form>",
  "services": {
    "<serviceCode>-<uuid>": {
      "serviceCode": "ec2Enhancement",
      "region": "us-east-2",
      "regionName": "US East (Ohio)",
      "serviceName": "Amazon EC2",
      "estimateFor": "template",
      "version": "0.0.68",
      "description": null,
      "calculationComponents": { ... service-specific input fields ... },
      "serviceCost":   { "monthly": 68.62, "upfront": 0 },
      "configSummary": "Tenancy (Shared Instances), ..."
    },
    ...
  },
  "groups": {},
  "groupSubtotal": { "monthly": 1828.44, "upfront": 0 },
  "totalCost":     { "monthly": 1828.44, "upfront": 0 },
  "support": {},
  "metaData": {
    "locale": "en_US",
    "currency": "USD",
    "createdOn": "2026-05-09T18:31:23.509Z",
    "source": "calculator-platform"
  }
}
```

`serviceCode` values seen in the captured estimate: `ec2Enhancement`, `amazonRDSPostgreSQLDB`, `amazonSimpleStorageServiceGroup`, `amazonVirtualPrivateCloud`. Group-style services (S3, VPC) use a `subServices` array with one mini line item per sub-feature; flat services put their inputs directly under `calculationComponents`.

The full captured body is preserved verbatim at `references/examples/sample-saveas-body.json` (365 lines, 4 services).

### Critical observation: pricing is computed client-side

The body the SPA sends to `saveAs` already contains the final `serviceCost` and `totalCost` numbers. The save endpoint does not validate or recompute them — it stores the JSON as-is. We confirmed this by stamping a fresh `metaData.createdOn` and a different `name`, then re-fetching the load URL: the loaded JSON was byte-for-byte the body we sent (with the server's pretty-print).

Implication for callers: any pricing math you want to be authoritative has to be done client-side before posting. Conversely, you have full control over what shows up in the saved estimate.

## Response schema

API Gateway Lambda-proxy envelope:

```json
{
  "statusCode": 201,
  "body": "{\"message\":\"The file name is <40hex>\",\"savedKey\":\"<40hex>\"}",
  "isBase64Encoded": false,
  "headers": { "Content-Type": "application/json", ... }
}
```

`savedKey` is 40 lowercase hex chars (SHA-1 length). The PoC computed SHA-1 of the raw captured body and got `d02adc36...` while the server returned `55bea3f0...` for the same body — so the server normalizes/re-serializes (or salts, or randomizes) before producing the key. Don't try to predict it; read it from the response.

## Share URL derivation

From `captures/bundle.js`:

```js
savedKey; ... e = r.replace(/(id=).*?(&|$)/, "id=" + savedKey + "$2")
```

The SPA takes its current URL and substitutes the `id=` query parameter. Since the SPA's route is `https://calculator.aws/#/estimate?id=...`, the share URL is:

```
https://calculator.aws/#/estimate?id=<savedKey>
```

## Reproduction

```bash
pip install requests
python scripts/create_estimate.py references/examples/sample-saveas-body.json
# → prints https://calculator.aws/#/estimate?id=<40hex>
```

Or with bare curl using the captured body verbatim:

```bash
curl -s -X POST https://dnd5zrqcec4or.cloudfront.net/Prod/v2/saveAs \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Origin: https://calculator.aws' \
  --data @references/examples/sample-saveas-body.json | jq -r '.body' | jq -r '.savedKey'
```

## Verification log

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| PoC prints a share URL on stdout, exit 0 | ✓ — `https://calculator.aws/#/estimate?id=491f7f59c4d962ebf2291d935b3ec3f3f1555eb7` |
| Two consecutive runs produce distinct savedKeys | ✓ — `491f7f59...` vs `48c734a5...` (server distinguishes by content; `metaData.createdOn` bumps every call) |
| Modifying the input changes the loaded output | ✓ — changed `name` to "PoC Mutation Test — aws-calc spike", round-tripped, loaded JSON reflected the new name and a new key (`9a42d981...`) |
| GET on the load endpoint returns the JSON we sent | ✓ — `HTTP 200`, 10 745 bytes, `totalCost.monthly: 1828.44` matches input |
| Share URL renders the estimate when opened in a browser | **manual** — open one of the keys above in a browser to confirm |
| `findings.md` complete with no TBDs | ✓ |

## Things still unknown / out of scope for this spike

- Whether `Origin: https://calculator.aws` is strictly required (not tested against a bare-headers POST).
- Whether identical bodies produce identical savedKeys (i.e. is the key a deterministic content hash?). Each PoC run bumped `createdOn`, so the hash differed every time.
- Rate-limit / WAF behavior under sustained load. CloudFront is almost certainly fronting AWS WAF; do not hammer this from automation.
- Whether the SPA recomputes prices from `calculationComponents` on load (and overrides the stored `serviceCost` / `totalCost`) or trusts the stored numbers. Browser-side check would settle this — `serviceCost` tampering would either be ignored on render, or persist visibly.
- The `prod-api.builder-ui.pricing-calculator.aws.a2z.com/v2/services` endpoint surfaced in the bundle but never fired during the captured public flow. Likely an internal builder/admin API.
